sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Cloud computing changes how an organization pays for computing resources. The objective is not simply to claim AWS is cheaper, but to recognize the economic mechanisms that can create financial advantages.
bullets: Aspects of cloud economics and potential cost savings
Fixed costs compared with variable costs
sections.callout: How can cloud computing change the way an organization spends money and uses resources?

sections.title: Cloud Economics
paragraphs: Cloud economics examines the financial considerations and economic benefits associated with cloud computing. Instead of owning and operating every physical component, organizations can consume cloud resources according to need.
sections.callout: How does the cloud change the money side of computing?

sections.title: Fixed Costs vs. Variable Costs

entries.title: Fixed Costs
paragraphs: A fixed cost remains even when the resource is lightly used. Purchased servers, equipment, and facility capacity cost money regardless of utilization.
entries.memoryHook: FIXED = stays. Own it and pay even when it is idle.

entries.title: Variable Costs
paragraphs: A variable cost changes according to consumption. Cloud spending can rise during busy periods and fall when less capacity is needed.
entries.memoryHook: VARIABLE = changes. Use more, pay more; use less, pay less.

sections.callout: Cloud can shift spending from large fixed infrastructure investments toward variable consumption-based costs.

sections.title: Costs Associated with On-Premises Environments
paragraphs: The purchase price of one server is not the complete cost of running on-premises infrastructure.
sections.callout: HARDWARE + FACILITY + POWER + COOLING + MAINTENANCE + PEOPLE + LICENSING

sections.title: Licensing Strategies

entries.title: Bring Your Own License (BYOL)
paragraphs: The organization uses an eligible software license it already owns with its cloud workload, subject to applicable license terms.
entries.memoryHook: I already have an eligible license.

entries.title: Included License
paragraphs: The software licensing cost is incorporated into the cloud resource or offering rather than supplied from an existing customer entitlement.

sections.callout: BRING IT → BYOL. COMES WITH IT → INCLUDED.

sections.title: Rightsizing
paragraphs: Rightsizing means matching resources to the workload's actual requirements. Consistently underused, overprovisioned capacity can create unnecessary cost.
bullets: Select appropriate compute, memory, storage, and performance
Avoid paying for capacity the workload does not need
sections.callout: NOT TOO BIG. NOT TOO SMALL. RIGHT SIZE.

sections.title: Benefits of Automation
paragraphs: Automation performs repeatable work without requiring the same manual effort each time. Human time and operational effort are also economic resources. AWS CloudFormation can provision and configure approved infrastructure repeatedly from a template.
sections.callout: MAKE THE COMPUTER DO THE REPEATABLE WORK

sections.title: Managed AWS Services
paragraphs: Managed services can reduce undifferentiated operational work because AWS operates more of the underlying service platform. The customer still configures access, data, and workload behavior according to the shared responsibility model.

entries.title: Amazon RDS
paragraphs: Managed relational database service.
entries.memoryHook: Relational database without managing the database platform alone.

entries.title: Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS
paragraphs: Managed container orchestration services for ECS containers and Kubernetes workloads.

entries.title: Amazon DynamoDB
paragraphs: Managed serverless NoSQL key-value and document database.

sections.callout: AWS MANAGES MORE OF THE PLATFORM → CUSTOMER TEAMS CAN FOCUS MORE ON THE WORKLOAD

sections.title: Economies of Scale
paragraphs: Economies of scale are financial efficiencies created by operating at very large scale. AWS aggregates demand and operates infrastructure for many customers, achieving efficiencies that a smaller individual organization may not obtain alone.

sections.title: Potential Cost Savings of Moving to Cloud
paragraphs: Moving to cloud is not automatically cheaper. Savings can result when an organization changes how it purchases, sizes, operates, and pays for infrastructure.
sections.callout: Understand why savings can occur—not a guarantee that every migration costs less.

entries.title: Fixed vs. Variable Cost
paragraphs: Pay regardless of utilization → Fixed. Cost changes with consumption → Variable.

entries.title: BYOL vs. Included License
paragraphs: Customer supplies an eligible existing license → BYOL. License is incorporated into the offering → Included license.

entries.title: Rightsizing vs. Elasticity
paragraphs: Choose an appropriately sized resource → Rightsizing. Increase or decrease resources as demand changes → Elasticity.

entries.title: Rightsizing vs. Cost Optimization
paragraphs: Specific resource-sizing action → Rightsizing. Well-Architected financial-efficiency pillar → Cost Optimization.

entries.title: Automation vs. Agility
paragraphs: Perform repeatable tasks automatically → Automation. Experiment, adapt, and respond quickly → Agility.

entries.title: Managed Service vs. Self-Managed Workload
paragraphs: AWS operates more of the service platform → Managed service. The customer installs and operates the software stack on compute → Self-managed workload.

entries.title: Economies of Scale vs. Elasticity
paragraphs: Provider scale creates economic efficiency → Economies of scale. Workload capacity changes with demand → Elasticity.
